method.purpose: Mechanism diagnosis only, not release acceptance and not retries until green.
method.benchmark: AST-extracted actual tests/e2e/game.spec.ts page.evaluate callback; all fixture values, warm-ups, call order and counts retained. Wrapper adds UserTiming marks and chronological choice/RNG/heap data. Context Playwright tracing mirrors retain-on-failure capture. Browser CDP trace is additional instrumentation.
method.conditioning: Six fresh contexts in one reused browser: actual first cover E2E and first five game E2Es, all current UI, same source callbacks; artifact writes redirected to owned .tmp. No audio/codex/combat/flow suite prefix; NOT the complete 14-test suite.
method.legacy: Only benchmark page serves git HEAD header/home bodies and omits new home.css main import, via request routing. Other modules untouched; current and legacy use identical route/fetch paths.
limitations: Three predetermined cases; UI comparison is not counterbalanced and gives no statistical upper-bound inference.
Instrumentation and isolated existing-server port override can perturb timings.
Per-process CPU deltas are coarse; absence of a sampled competing process does not prove absence of OS preemption.
V8 main-thread compilation/GC overlap supports attribution of observed diagnostic calls only, not historic failures without engine traces.
No forced GC, no extra AI warm-up, no altered gameplay, thresholds, retries, optimization flags or production sources.
Two completed current-UI cases only: the legacy case never reached benchmark. These data cannot establish zero UI effect.

Tracing.start introduced a variable pre-benchmark delay (about 1s fresh versus about 11s conditioned, inferred from the template actionTime); tier/heap preparation was not identical. Engine tracing itself may add significant overhead.

The initial exact-URL request routes did not match Vite timestamp query strings on templates in these current-UI cases. The retained current sources were loaded normally; legacy was never measured. Future route matchers have been corrected but not browser-validated.

incompleteCases.reason: Outer shell 150-second bound expired during third prelude; no benchmark result/engine trace. Not rerun.

systemSummary.caveat: Sampler used Math.Max(0,double), which PowerShell resolved through an integer overload: process CPU deltas were rounded to whole seconds. Sampling also slowed to roughly 0.5-2s. The displayed aggregate CPU percentages cannot clear or convict system load. Sampler fixed for future use only; no remeasurement.

conclusion.status: Root cause unconfirmed; bounded diagnosis stopped without changes to gameplay/tests/thresholds.
confirmed: Full-suite failures remain valid; isolated passes do not clear them.
Current traced fresh and conditioned cases both have spikes; no evidence that suite accumulation is a necessary cause.
Recorded GC and direct JIT scope durations are too short to explain most of the largest diagnostic spike.
conclusion.nextSeparateTask: Dedicated performance task: fixed-count fresh/current versus HEAD-home paired runs, with equalized time since launch and explicit low-overhead function CPU profiles plus deoptimization reasons. Collect scheduling/frequency evidence only if thread-CPU gaps warrant it. Keep the 100ms gate and all gameplay rules unchanged; do not add warm-ups/retries as a workaround.
conclusion.releaseScope: Cover UX/unit/layout/production-offline acceptance is independent of the still-failed full E2E performance gate; this report is not release acceptance.

findings.actualFixtureIsolation: Installed Playwright 1.64.1 has worker-scoped browser, default non-reused context and new page per test. One worker/fullyParallel false. Thus prior save/DOM are not directly shared, but browser services/resources and the operating system are. This alone does not prove renderer-isolate reuse or heap leakage.
findings.benchmarkSampling: Master=one warm-up+10 samples, then levels 0,1,2,3 each one warm-up+5 samples on the same pressure state/RNG, then advantage one warm-up+5. All maxima are small-sample wall-time maxima, not steady-state or worst-case bounds. Normal/hard forecast work differs from master; fast master is not proof hard has budget.
findings.pressureComparison: Canonical comparison includes config/team/RNG and forecast-relevant unit fields. Complete snapshot hashes differ only in inherited, forecast-unused actionTime; canonical hash equal. All observed AI choices and RNG sequences match between the two completed cases.
findings.observed: Under additional engine instrumentation a fresh browser also spikes (measured hard max 207.6ms); conditioned max 100.9ms. Conditioning warm-up (not counted in gate) was 122.5ms. This is not an uninstrumented full-suite/isolated A/B and must not replace original failures.
findings.narrowExclusions: Fresh call 32 spans 207.540ms, including 181.810ms main-thread CPU. Main-thread GC overlap is 9.442ms and JIT-labelled scope overlap 1.091ms. Therefore a 150ms stop-the-world GC or a 150ms directly recorded synchronous compilation pause does NOT explain this diagnostic spike. The wall-minus-thread-CPU gap is about 25.7ms, not the bulk of the spike.
findings.unresolved: Remaining CPU is not function-attributed. V8 tiering/deoptimization/slow-path execution is a lead, not a proven cause; tracing overhead, changes in executed work and CPU frequency remain possible. No function names/deoptimization reasons, CPU profile or ETW scheduling trace were collected. Historical 182.5/163.7ms spikes have no V8 traces.
findings.uiImpact: Unresolved: old-home benchmark never completed; untouched core hashes establish unchanged code only, not unchanged browser performance.
